personality_one_liner: A modern, clean, and trustworthy healthcare experience with clear typography, intuitive navigation, and calming blue tones for all age groups.

spacing.rule: Use generous vertical breathing room for clarity. Forms and cards should be well spaced, accommodating larger touch targets for accessibility.

do's: Use on the bottom tab bar when content scrolls behind
Use for the Patient 'Upcoming Appointment' hero card overlay
Sticky headers in the Doctor and Receptionist dashboards
dont's: Avoid on form inputs or dense lists like Patient History
Do not over-blur; ensure high contrast for older demographics

screens.name: Auth
screens.purpose: Simple role selection for Patient, Doctor, or Receptionist to enter their respective flows.
screens.layout: Minimalist center-aligned stack of 3 large Pill buttons for each role. A healthcare cross or clinic logo at the top.

screens.name: PatientHome
screens.purpose: Help patient find a doctor and view upcoming active bookings.
screens.layout: Top: Greeting and search bar (specialty, doctor name, city). Below: Glassmorphic 'Upcoming Appointment' hero card featuring the clinic_waiting_room image as background with dark gradient scrim. Below: Grid of specialties (Cardiology, Dental, etc.) using tinted icon containers.

screens.name: DoctorProfile
screens.purpose: Provide trust signals and essential details (fees, timings, wait time) before booking.
screens.layout: Hero: large image of the doctor (doctor_portrait), name, rating. Middle: concise info cards for 'Fees', 'Consultation Timings', 'Avg Wait Time'. Bottom: Sticky 'Book Appointment' CTA at the bottom above safe area.

screens.name: PatientBooking
screens.purpose: Date, time selection and mock payment.
screens.layout: Horizontal scrolling calendar pills for dates. Grid of time slots inside chips (surfaceTertiary for inactive, brandPrimary for selected). Mock payment sheet slides up on confirmation.

screens.name: PatientLiveQueue
screens.purpose: Real-time queue tracking to reduce anxiety in the waiting room.

states.error: Lost connection to clinic live queue

screens.layout: Dashboard feel. Top: Massive 'You are #8' typography. Middle: ETA (e.g., '~45 mins'), 'Currently serving #5', and progress bar. Bottom: Primary action 'Refresh' or 'Leave Queue'.

screens.name: ReceptionistDashboard
screens.purpose: Operational queue management for front desk to process arrivals quickly.
screens.layout: List view of today's patients ordered by token number. Each row has patient name, token, and a swipe-to-action or dropdown to 'Mark Arrived', 'Start', 'Complete', or 'Skip'. Floating Action Button for 'Emergency Insert'.

screens.name: DoctorDashboard
screens.purpose: Task-first clinical dashboard to see who is next and manage shift status.
screens.layout: Top: 3-way segmented control for status (Active, Pause/Break, Emergency). KPI Row (Total, Pending, Completed). List of the next 3-5 patients prominently displayed with a 'Call Next' primary button inside the top patient's card.

doctor_portrait.alt: Indian male doctor in blue scrubs

instructions_to_main_agent: Adhere strictly to the Plus Jakarta Sans font with max 500 weight. Hierarchy must be established entirely through font sizes and spacing.
For 'PatientLiveQueue', ensure the current number 'You are #8' uses 3xl or larger font size so it is readable from a distance.
Implement the 'PatientHome' hero card with a gradient scrim layered over the `clinic_waiting_room` image to ensure text overlay contrast.
Ensure 'DoctorProfile' features the `doctor_portrait` image prominently at the top with a soft fade at the bottom edge.
Keep navigation simple: use bottom tabs for patient (Home, Queue, History) but single-screen stacks for Doctor and Receptionist dashboard to minimize clicks.
Any bottom CTA like 'Book Appointment' must be fixed/sticky above the safe area while the content scrolls underneath.
